subsystems.scoring: Fixed heading and fixed elevation; powered back roller controls spin. Team accepted a bounded shooting area around the tarmac.

subsystems.controls: Driver feedback and repeatable shot locations reduce aiming complexity.

versions: Offseason collector and fast climb shown in Chezy interview; do not assume those timings at early events.

context_documents.body:
# 2022-2046: A bounded shooting envelope can be an intentional simplification

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The collector moves from early flap/Velcro contacts through rubber to a later griptape tube. Breakaway members protect the core. A fixed-heading, fixed-elevation launcher uses a powered back roller and accepts a bounded shooting region; the climb uses swing to reach traversal.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source explicitly reports early contacts repelling cargo and later material experiments. The retained account treats the limited shooting area as an accepted design constraint.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Range is not free capability. A simpler scorer can be effective if its reachable positions, acquisition routes and defended access remain adequate. Offseason material changes must not be back-projected onto Worlds.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test access to the preferred scoring area under defense and compare collector materials with consistent cargo and approach speed.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
